documents.title: Hearing: Department of the Navy Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Request Committee on Armed Services

witnesses.name: The Honorable Hung Cao
witnesses.position: Acting Secretary of the Navy, Department of the Navy

witnesses.name: Admiral Daryl Caudle
witnesses.position: Chief of Naval Operations, United States Navy

witnesses.name: General Eric M. Smith
witnesses.position: Commandant, United States Marine Corps

events.evidence_span: Defending the homeland and the American people—whether at the land borders or across the maritime approaches—remains the Marine Corps' top priority as the Nation's premier expeditionary force-in-readiness. At the same time the Indo-Pacific remains the region where military competition is most intense and where strategic risk is most concentrated.
events.statement: The Marine Corps says defending the homeland is its top priority, while also treating the Indo-Pacific as its most consequential theater.

events.evidence_span: To ensure the Corps remains the Nation's premier expeditionary force in readiness—capable of deterring, responding, and winning in any clime or place—we are focused on: restoring a 3.0 Amphibious Ready Group and Marine Expeditionary Unit presence, setting the theater, accelerating modernization and lethality, and building and sustaining a lethal force.
events.statement: The Corps says it is focused on restoring a 3.0 ARG/MEU presence, setting the theater, accelerating modernization and lethality, and building and sustaining a lethal force.

events.evidence_span: This year's President's Budget allows us to sustain this momentum. A "generational investment," the President's Budget for Fiscal Year 2027 (PB27) provides monumental investment in Amphibious Warfare Ships and Medium Landing Ships, revolutionizes our logistics enterprise to sustain distributed forces, accelerates our modernization and lethality efforts by years, and greatly enhances the Quality of Life for our Marines and Sailors.
events.statement: The President's Budget for Fiscal Year 2027 is described as a generational investment that funds amphibious warfare ships, medium landing ships, logistics, modernization, and quality of life improvements.

events.evidence_span: My best military advice is that a continuous 3.0 ARG/MEU presence is required to provide Geographic Combatant Commanders, and our Nation, with the forces they need to meet the challenges presented across the globe. A 3.0 ARG/MEU presence means three continuously forward deployed ARG/MEU teams, one sourced from the East Coast, one from the West Coast, and one forward stationed from Okinawa.
events.statement: The Marine Corps says a continuous 3.0 ARG/MEU presence is required and that each team needs at least three amphibious warfare ships.

events.evidence_span: While the Medium Landing Ship will arrive later than originally planned, recent decisions have restored momentum and set conditions for fielding the first vessels in the coming decade.
events.statement: The Medium Landing Ship will arrive later than originally planned, though the Corps says recent decisions have restored momentum.

events.evidence_span: Until the Medium Landing Ship is fielded in sufficient numbers, the Littoral Maneuver Bridging Strategy provides a necessary near-term solution to address critical mobility gaps. The strategy integrates contractor owned/contractor operated chartered vessels, hybrid-crewed expeditionary fast transport platforms, experimentation efforts, and selective modernization to sustain operational mobility for stand-in and forward-deployed forces.
events.statement: Until the Medium Landing Ship is fielded in sufficient numbers, the Corps is using the Littoral Maneuver Bridging Strategy as a near-term workaround for mobility gaps.

events.evidence_span: A family of connectors remains essential to sustaining littoral mobility across diverse operational conditions. Platforms such as the Autonomous Low-Profile Vessel, Multi-Mission Reconnaissance Craft, and LCU 1710 provide complementary capabilities that enable tactical maneuver, logistics distribution, and reconnaissance in shallow and austere environments.
events.program: Autonomous Low-Profile Vessel, Multi-Mission Reconnaissance Craft, and LCU 1710
events.statement: The Corps says it is working to field the Autonomous Low-Profile Vessel, Multi-Mission Reconnaissance Craft, and LCU 1710 to expand connector capacity.

events.statement: Sen. Todd Young is scheduled to appear on stage at the Wednesday event.

events.evidence_span: "A Taiwan scenario is not the only place where that type of capability would be needed. You might think of that in any choke point. That may be a capability I'd want in the [strait] there at the end of the Red Sea or in the Strait of Hormuz or anywhere else," Adm. Caudle said.
events.statement: Adm. Caudle said the Navy would need a tailored set of unmanned forces for choke points and contested maritime areas.

events.evidence_span: A key topic will be the Trump administration's Golden Fleet, an ambitious plan to build dozens of new vessels with $65.8 billion earmarked in the proposed fiscal 2027 budget.
events.statement: The Trump administration's proposed fiscal 2027 budget earmarks $65.8 billion for the Golden Fleet shipbuilding plan.

events.evidence_span: The Pentagon is seeking $54.6 billion for its Defense Autonomous Warfare Group, the umbrella initiative overseeing the effort to produce and field drones in large numbers.
events.statement: The Pentagon is seeking $54.6 billion for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group to produce and field drones in large numbers.

events.evidence_span: In a recent report to Congress obtained by Threat Status, Adm. Paparo said he wants at least $2.3 billion specifically for maritime, underwater and ground-based drone weapons in the Pacific.
events.statement: Adm. Paparo wants at least $2.3 billion for maritime, underwater and ground-based drone weapons in the Pacific.

documents.title: America's naval power transformation to be in spotlight at major Threat Status event

events.evidence_span: On May 11, 2026, the Department released its Fiscal Year 2027 Shipbuilding Plan, requesting $65.8 billion — a nearly 57% increase over last year — and outlining a 30-year roadmap to expand fleet capacity, revitalize the maritime industrial base, and deliver a more capable, ready, and lethal naval force.
events.statement: The Department of the Navy said its Fiscal Year 2027 Shipbuilding Plan requests $65.8 billion, nearly 57% more than last year.

events.evidence_span: The president is rightly recognizing that we need a renaissance and a resurgent sea and shipbuilding in our country," Admiral Caudle told Threat Status. "You're going to see an all hands on deck approach with modular shipbuilding as the core of the design change.
events.statement: Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle said the Navy will use an all-hands-on-deck approach with modular shipbuilding as the core of its future industrial strategy.

events.statement: The Navy said it needs to expand fleet capacity and revitalize the maritime industrial base to build a more capable, ready, and lethal naval force.
